items.title: Steve Turré interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 29, 2021
items.q: my parents took me to the Oakland Auditorium to see Duke Ellington... hearing that just blew my mind

ctx.x: In the mid-60s, there was so much music going on in the pop world and in the jazz world, and you were in an area known for innovations in rock music. And I wonder if there was a time when you considered that music as a career?

Not as a career, no. But I enjoyed it and I played it too, but you know jazz had my heart from an early age, early age. You know my mom and dad met at a Count Basie dance. And we had big band music, that was the dance music of their day you know. So you know we had big band music in the house all the time and I used to watch the Ed Sullivan Show and I saw Dizzy and Bird on there, I saw Louis Armstrong many times, as well as all the other great R&B and pop acts too. So I enjoyed all kinds of music. They had Nat…

So hearing that just blew my mind you know. I didn’t know what they were doing but it went boing — you know something big. And so it had my heart, from that age. But then in high school I heard James Brown and I used to have a little crystal radio set. I don’t know if you know what that is, but you —
